# AF 第三章 原文（重制基线）

## Chapter 3

[P01] How they worked and sweated（出汗了） to get the hay（干草） in! But their work brought good results, for the harvest was even bigger than they had hoped. Sometimes the work was hard; the tools were made for humans, not for animals, and it was a big problem that no animal could use any tool that meant standing on his back legs. But the pigs were so clever that they could find a way around every problem. As for the horses, they knew every part of the field, and in fact they understood mowing（割草） and raking（耙草） far better than Jones and his men ever did.

[P02] The pigs did not work. They told the others what to do and watched. They knew more, so it was natural for them to lead. Boxer and Clover pulled the cutter（切割机） or the horse-rake（耙子） and went round and round the field. A pig walked behind and called out "Gee（驾） up, comrade（同志）!" or "Whoa（停） back, comrade!" as needed. Every animal helped turn the hay and gather（收集） it. Even the ducks and hens worked all day, carrying small bits of hay in their beaks（鸟嘴）.

[P03] In the end they finished the harvest two days faster than Jones and his men usually did. Moreover, it was the biggest harvest the farm had ever seen. The hens and ducks picked up the very last stalk（茎）. No animal had stolen even a mouthful（一口）. No animal could use any tool that needed standing on his hind（后面的） legs, but they found a way round every difficulty. The pigs supervised（监督） and led the way. The cutter, rake, gee（驾） and whoa（停） went down to the humblest（最卑微） wisp（小捆） of stalk. All that summer the farm work went like clockwork（钟表）.

[P04] The animals were happy as never before. Every bite of food was a real joy, because it was their own food, made by themselves, not given by a mean master. With the useless（无用） humans gone, there was more to eat and more free time. They had many problems—when they gathered（聚集） the corn, they had to walk on it and blow the chaff（谷壳） away, because the farm had no threshing（打谷） machine—but the pigs, with their cleverness（聪明）, and Boxer, with his tremendous（极大的） muscles（肌肉）, always got them through.

[P05] Boxer was admired by everyone. He had been a hard worker even in Jones's time, but now he seemed more like three horses than one. Some days, all the work of the farm seemed to rest on his strong shoulders. From morning to night he pushed and pulled, always where the work was hardest. He had made a plan with one of the young roosters（公鸡） to wake him half an hour earlier than anyone else. Then he did extra（额外） work on whatever was most needed before the day's work began. His answer to every problem, every setback（挫折）, was "I will work harder!" He had made this his own motto. But everyone worked as much as he could.

[P06] The hens and ducks, for example, saved five bushels（蒲式耳） of corn at harvest by picking up loose（松的） grains（谷物）. Nobody stole, nobody complained about food, and the arguing and biting of the old days had almost gone. Nobody was idle—or almost nobody. Mollie was not good at getting up early, and often left work early, saying she had a stone in her hoof（蹄）. And the cat acted strangely. When there was work to do, the cat could never be found.

[P07] She would disappear for hours, then come back at meal-times, or in the evening after work, as if nothing had happened. But she always gave such good excuses, and purred（咕噜叫） so warmly, that no one could doubt her good intentions（意图）. Old Benjamin, the donkey, seemed the same as before the uprising（起义）. He did his work in the same slow, stubborn（固执） way as in Jones's time, never avoiding work and never asking for more. About the uprising and what came of it, he said nothing. When asked if he was happier now that Jones was gone, he would only say, "Donkeys live a long time.

[P08] None of you has ever seen a dead donkey," and the others had to accept this strange answer. He would only say, "Donkeys live a long time. None of you has ever seen a dead donkey," and the others had to accept this strange answer. On Sundays there was no work. Breakfast came an hour later than usual, and after breakfast there was a ceremony every week without fail. First they put up the flag. Snowball had found an old green tablecloth（桌布） of Mrs. Jones's in the harness（马具）-room and had painted a hoof and a horn on it in white.

[P09] Every Sunday morning, this flag went up the flagpole（旗杆） in the garden of the farmhouse（农舍）. The flag was green, Snowball said, to stand for the green fields of England, and the hoof and horn meant the future Republic（共和国） of the Animals, after the human race was beaten at last. After the flag went up, all the animals walked into the big barn（谷仓） for a big meeting called the Meeting. Here they planned the next week's work and put forward ideas to talk about. It was always the pigs who gave the ideas. The other animals knew how to vote, but could never think of any ideas of their own.

[P10] Snowball and Napoleon were the most active in the debates. But everyone saw that these two never agreed: if one made a suggestion, the other would always oppose（反对） it. Even when they agreed—something no one could argue about—to set aside（旁边） the small field behind the orchard（果园） as a resting place for animals too old to work, they had a stormy（暴风雨） debate about the right retiring（退休） age for each kind of animal. The Meeting always ended with the song 'animals of England', and the afternoon was free for play. The pigs had set aside the harness-room（挽具室） as a headquarters（总部） for themselves.

[P11] In the evenings, they studied blacksmithing（打铁）, carpentering（木工活）, and other skills from books taken from the farmhouse. Snowball also formed Animal Committees（委员会） for the animals. He made the Egg Production Committee（委员会） for the hens, the Clean Tails League（联盟） for the cows, the Wild Comrades（同志们）' Re-education Committee（委员会） to tame（驯服） rats and rabbits, the Whiter Wool（羊毛） Movement for the sheep, and more, and he started classes in reading and writing. Most of these projects failed. The plan to tame wild creatures（生物） fell apart（分开） almost at once.

[P12] They went on as before, and used any kindness. The cat joined the Re-education Committee and worked hard for a few days. One day she was on a roof, talking to some sparrows（麻雀） just out of reach. She told them all animals were now comrades（同志们）, and any sparrow（麻雀） could sit on her paw（爪子）. But the sparrows stayed away. The reading and writing classes did very well. By autumn almost every animal could read and write a little. As for the pigs, they could already read and write perfectly.

[P13] The dogs learned to read quite well, but they only cared about the Seven Commandments（戒律）. Muriel, the goat, could read a little better than the dogs. Sometimes she read to the others from old newspaper on the rubbish heap（堆）. Benjamin could read as well as any pig, but he never did. He said nothing was worth reading. Clover learned the whole alphabet（字母表）, but she could not put words together. Boxer could not get past the letter D. He would trace（痕迹） out A, B, C, D in the dust（灰尘） with his big hoof, then stand and stare（盯着） at the letters. Sometimes he shook his forelock（额发）, trying hard to remember what came next, and never succeeding.

[P14] Sometimes he did learn E, F, G, H. But then he always found he had forgotten A, B, C, and D. In the end he decided to be happy with the first four letters. He wrote them out once or twice every day to help his memory. Mollie would not learn any letters but the six that spelt（拼写） her own name. She made these neatly（整洁地） out of small twigs（细枝）. Then she put a flower or two on them and walked round them, admiring her work.

[P15] It was also found that stupider animals, like sheep, hens, and ducks, could not learn the Seven Commandments（戒律） by heart. After much thought Snowball said they could be put into one short saying: "Four legs good, two legs bad." He said this held the main rule of Animalism（动物主义）. Anyone who understood it would be safe from human influences. The birds first objected, because it seemed they also had two legs, but Snowball showed them they did not. But Snowball proved this was not true. "A bird's wing, comrades," he said, "is an organ（器官） of propulsion（推进） and not of manipulation（操作）."

[P16] So a wing should be called a leg. What makes man different is the HAND, the tool he uses to do bad things." The birds did not understand Snowball's long words, but they accepted what he said, and all the simpler animals began to learn the new saying by heart. FOUR LEGS GOOD, TWO LEGS BAD was written on the end wall of the barn, above the Seven Commandments and in bigger letters. The sheep liked this saying very much, and often as they lay in the field they would all start bleating"Four legs good, two legs bad!"

[P17] "Four legs good, two legs bad!" and they would keep it up for hours, never getting tired of it. Napoleon did not care about Snowball's committees（委员会）. He said teaching the young was more important than anything done for the grown-up animals. Jessie and Bluebell had both had puppies soon after the hay harvest, and they gave birth to nine strong puppies. As soon as they stopped drinking their mother's milk, Napoleon took them away. He said he would take charge（冲锋） of their education himself. He took them up to a loft（阁楼） reached only by a ladder from the harness-room, and kept them hidden there. Soon the rest of the farm forgot they were there. The mystery of where the milk went was soon cleared up.

[P18] It was mixed into the pigs' mash（糊状饲料） every day. The early apples were ripe（成熟） now, and the orchard grass was covered with windfalls（落果）. The animals had thought these would be shared equally. One day, the order came that all the windfalls must be collected and brought to the harness-room（挽具室） for the pigs. Some animals murmured（低语）, but it was no use. All the pigs agreed, even Snowball and Napoleon. Squealer was sent to explain. "Comrades!" he cried.

[P19] "You do not think, I hope, that we pigs do this because we are selfish and want special rights? Many of us do not even like milk and apples. We take these things only to keep healthy. Milk and apples, comrades, hold things that a pig truly needs to stay well. We pigs are brainworkers（脑力劳动者）. All the managing and planning of this farm rests on us. Day and night we watch over your good. It is for YOUR sake（利益） that we drink that milk and eat those apples. Do you know what would happen if we pigs failed in our duty?

[P20] Jones would come back! Yes, Jones would come back! "Surely, comrades," cried Squealer, almost begging（乞求）, jumping from side to side and moving his tail, "surely none of you wants to see Jones come back?"

Now if there was one thing the animals were sure of, it was that they did not want Jones back. When they saw it this way, they had nothing more to say. Keeping the pigs healthy was too clear to question. So they agreed without more argument（争论） that the milk and the fallen apples (and also the main apple crop when it was ripe) should be kept for the pigs alone.
